label: Control bar
description: The two rows above a result list: the results header ('N results' and Save filters) and the bulk action bar (select-all checkbox, Sort immediately after it, then Edit / Move to catalog / Delete / Export selection).

slots.results-header: '{{result_count}} results' at 24px on the left, a secondary 'Save filters' button on the right.
slots.bulk-bar: A select-all checkbox, the sort control as text immediately after it, then the four bulk-action verbs (Edit / Move to catalog / Delete / Export selection) as plain-text buttons, in that order, matching the product row.

renderNotes: Two sibling frames, spliced in this order; the DIVIDER that follows them belongs to the page recipe.
checkbox renders no label element when Label is the empty string (Task 1.2).

button's variant here (`Type=Secondary, State=Default` for Save filters; `Type=Tertiary, State=Default` for the four bulk verbs) is the renderer's legacy Type axis (ds-html-map.js button case, typeMap fallback), not the Intent/Emphasis/Size/State axis pair the authoring doc's vocabulary table documents as current; both are read by the same case, so this is a deliberate, working choice, not a stale example. Type=Tertiary paints `background: transparent` with no visible border (ds-base.css), which is the closest built equivalent to the capture's plain-text bulk verbs.

Review round 2 (Important, plan defect): the bulk bar previously drew a `toolbar` instance, which the product does not have here (it draws Filter/Sort/View/More icons instead, and dropped the four verbs the product actually shows). Removed. No DS-tier bulk-action-bar leaf exists at all (checked ds-components-authoring.md's vocabulary table), so the four verbs are carried as `button Type=Tertiary` leaves, capture content rather than placeholders (the product always shows these same four words on this row), until a dedicated component ships -- a follow-up, not done here.
This section's own {{...}} placeholders: {{result_count}} (also used independently by the page recipe's rail) and {{sort_label}}.
